title: Ops SLO cadence protocol & stakeholder roles (compact plan)
body:
Purpose:
This compact doc defines a lightweight, practical SLO cadence protocol for cross-functional teams and a clear stakeholder roles compact. It's intended for short-term operational adoption across Model Serving, Dedicated, Console, and Customer Success teams — not a heavy governance doc.

Scope & intent:
- Focus: service-level objectives for inference endpoints (hosted API + dedicated pools). Not for infra-only GC/cluster metrics (those will be referenced).
- Timebox: pilot for 90 days (Feb–Apr 2026).
- Deliverable: an operational cadence (weekly + monthly rituals), a minimal runbook template, role commitments, and measurable acceptance criteria to inform scaling to the wider org.

Goals (what success looks like):
1) Teams adopt a 3-step SLO cadence: weekly signal review, monthly SLO review, quarterly SLO calibration.
2) SRE partnership model reduces Sev->Pager escalations attributable to unclear SLO ownership by 40% in pilot teams.
3) All participating services publish: SLI definition doc, single SLO, and an error-budget policy in the team runbook.
4) A lightweight automation (dashboard) surfaces top-3 SLO regressions every day.

Key metrics to track (pilot):
- Number of services with published SLI/SLO/error-budget (target 12/12 for pilot teams).
- Weekly signal review attendance rate (target >=80%).
- Time from SLO breach to mitigation plan (target <= 4 hours for high severity).
- Reduction in customer-impacting incidents linked to regression (target 30% lower).

Principles (keeps us pragmatic):
- Keep it short: one page SLO spec per service.
- One owner per SLO (can be role not person) and one SRE partner.
- Use the simplest SLI that maps to customer experience (p95 latency for lower-latency endpoints, success rate for routing/availability).
- Error budget is permission: when budget is exhausted, devs and SREs must implement one agreed action within the next sprint.

Stakeholder compact (roles & responsibilities):
- Service/Product Owner (PO): owns the customer promise; defines target SLO; signs off on runbook actions.
- Platform SRE (SRE partner): validates SLI instrumentation, owns alert thresholds for signal review, facilitates mitigation/war room.
- Infra/Capacity Lead: ensures reserved capacity and scaling policies are compatible with SLOs (Dedicated).
- Observability/Console Owner: builds dashboard slices and ensures daily regression emails exist.
- Solutions/CS representative: provides customer impact context; triages customer-facing severity.

Decision rhythm (cadence):
- Daily: automated SLO digest email (top 3 regressions) to SRE/PO/infra. No live meeting; if a regression appears, the SRE partner flags a triage.
- Weekly (30–45 min): signal review. Attendees: PO, SRE partner, infra lead, oncall engineer. Agenda: review weekly SLI trends, open incidents, action items.
- Monthly (60 min): SLO review. Attendees: PO, SRE partner, product PM, observability owner. Agenda: validate assumptions, re-evaluate SLO targets if usage/traffic changed, decide runbook changes.
- Quarterly: calibration workshop across services (90 min) to align SLO taxonomy, share learnings.

Operational artifacts (templates):
- One-page SLO spec (required fields): service name; user-facing intent; SLI metric + query; SLO target and window; error-budget policy (what to do when exhausted); owner and SRE partner; runbook link.
- Signal review notes template (checkboxes for regressions): observed metric, timestamp, probable root cause, immediate mitigation, planned fix, owner, ETA.
- Runbook minimal sections: detection, quick mitigation steps, rollback plan, post-mortem trigger conditions, who-to-pager.

90-day pilot sprint map (high level):
- Week 0 (Feb week 1): kickoff + alignment workshop. Goal: onboard 4 pilot services, draft one-page SLO specs.
- Weeks 1–4: instrument SLIs where missing, validate dashboards, wire daily digest.
- Weeks 5–8: run weekly signal reviews, iterate runbooks; mid-pilot health check (metrics).
- Weeks 9–12: SLO review + calibration; collect feedback; produce adoption playbook for org.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: signal overload -> too many false regressions. Mitigation: tune SLI query windows and require >=2 datapoints before flagging; implement severity buckets.
- Risk: ownership ambiguity -> missed runbook updates. Mitigation: SLO spec must include owner + secondary; tie to team OKRs for accountability.
- Risk: capacity mismatch under burst -> error budget drain. Mitigation: infra lead to publish burst policy and reserve burst capacity for pilot.

Escalation ladder (compact):
1) On-call engineer handles immediate mitigation (15–60 min).
2) SRE partner runs war room if mitigation not effective within 60m.
3) PO and infra lead informed within 2 hours for potential customer communications.

Acceptance criteria for pilot completion:
- All pilot services have one-page SLO spec in Confluence and runbook linked.
- Daily digest and weekly signal review meeting established with >75% attendance.
- At least 2 incident-to-SLO feedback loop entries created (postmortems referencing SLO changes).
- Playbook draft (this doc expanded to 4 pages) created for org rollout.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Should we allow different SLI aggregation windows per service? (likely yes, but standard defaults are needed).
- Who pays for extra dedicated capacity for pilot bursts? Need finance sign-off.
- Automation: build a flag in console to mark a service as 'pilot SLO' so dashboards auto-include it. Owner: observability team.

Immediate next steps (today-week):
1) Send this compact plan to pilot stakeholders and attach to SRE-7890 (Jira).
2) Kickoff workshop: schedule 60min session in the next 5 working days — invite PO, SRE partner, infra lead, obs owner, CS rep.
3) Create Confluence page with one-page SLO spec template and example for inference-hosting-api.

Quick reference contact list:
- Aditi Kapoor (owner) — aditi@redwood.ai
- Miguel Torres (SRE partner) — miguel@redwood.ai
- Sana Ahmed (Observability) — sana@redwood.ai

Notes (informal):
- Keep the templates so teams can copy/paste; don't force centralized tooling yet. We want quick wins.
- If this pilot shows >60% reduction in customer-impacting regressions, push for org-wide cadence by Q3 2026.
- TODO: draft the daily digest format (json -> email) and get infra's buy-in for cost.

End of doc.
